title: Unary counit substitution and comparison transpose
statement:
Let $\mathcal C_s,\mathcal D_s,\mathcal C_t,\mathcal D_t$ be categories [def-nagata-category]. For $i=s,t$ specify functors $R_i:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal D_i$ and $L_i:\mathcal D_i\to\mathcal C_i$ and natural transformations $u_i:1\to L_iR_i$, $e_i:R_iL_i\to1$ satisfying $L_i(e_{i,M})u_{i,L_iM}=1$ and $e_{i,R_iI}R_i(u_{i,I})=1$; these specify the adjunction $R_i\dashv L_i$. Composition below is right to left. Let $A:\mathcal D_s\to\mathcal D_t$, $\bar A:\mathcal C_s\to\mathcal C_t$ be functors, with a specified natural isomorphism $d_I:L_tAR_sI\xrightarrow{\sim}\bar AI$. Put $r_I=e_{t,AR_sI}R_t(d_I^{-1})$.

For any $I\in\mathcal C_s$, $M\in\mathcal D_s$ and $q:R_sI\to M$, set $b=L_s(q)u_{s,I}$ and $q_A=A(q)r_I$. Then
$$q=e_{s,M}R_s(b),\qquad L_t(r_I)u_{t,\bar AI}=d_I^{-1},$$
$$b_A:=L_t(q_A)u_{t,\bar AI}=L_tA(q)d_I^{-1}=L_tA(e_{s,M})d_{L_sM}^{-1}\bar A(b).$$
If $b$ and $e_{s,M}$ are invertible, $b_A$ is invertible and, for $a_A(M)=d_{L_sM}(L_tA(e_{s,M}))^{-1}$,
$$b_A^{-1}=\bar A(b^{-1})a_A(M).$$
For arbitrary $f:M\to M'$ with both $e_{s,M}$ and $e_{s,M'}$ invertible, the inverse-factor and comparison naturality identities are
$$ (L_tA(e_{s,M'}))^{-1}L_tA(f)=L_tAR_sL_s(f)(L_tA(e_{s,M}))^{-1},$$
$$a_A(M')L_tA(f)=\bar A(L_s(f))a_A(M).$$
For an identity coefficient map $q=1_{R_sI}$ its transpose is the actual $u_{s,I}$. If $e_{s,M}$ is invertible then $u_{s,L_sM}=L_s(e_{s,M})^{-1}$. If additionally an isomorphism $h:L_sR_sK\to K$ is given and $e_{s,R_sK}$ is invertible, then the actual $u_{s,K}$ is invertible and satisfies
$$u_{s,K}h=L_sR_s(h)u_{s,L_sR_sK}.$$
These are identities of morphisms in the given categories, without a faithfulness hypothesis on any auxiliary evaluation functor.

proof.text:
Use associativity and the identity laws of [def-nagata-category], and the functor and natural-transformation axioms in the hypotheses. Counit naturality at $q:R_sI\to M$ gives $e_{s,M}R_sL_s(q)=q e_{s,R_sI}$. Therefore
$$e_{s,M}R_s(b)=e_{s,M}R_sL_s(q)R_s(u_{s,I})=q e_{s,R_sI}R_s(u_{s,I})=q$$
by the stipulated triangle identity. No invertibility is used.

source.place: Coefficient comparisons preserve units and counits; agent-written unary component calculation from the specified naturality and triangle identities (Stacks 0037, definition-adjoint; 0GLL, lemma-unit-counit-relations). Calculation 1.

proof.text:
Apply unit naturality to $d_I^{-1}:\bar AI\to L_tAR_sI$:
$$L_tR_t(d_I^{-1})u_{t,\bar AI}=u_{t,L_tAR_sI}d_I^{-1}.$$
Apply $L_t$ to the definition of $r_I$ and substitute this equality. The other triangle identity, at $AR_sI\in\mathcal D_t$, gives
$$L_t(r_I)u_{t,\bar AI}=L_t(e_{t,AR_sI})u_{t,L_tAR_sI}d_I^{-1}=d_I^{-1}.$$

source.place: Coefficient comparisons preserve units and counits; agent-written unary component calculation from the specified naturality and triangle identities (Stacks 0037, definition-adjoint; 0GLL, lemma-unit-counit-relations). Calculation 2.

proof.text:
Expand $q_A=A(q)r_I$ and apply functoriality and step 2:
$$b_A=L_t(q_A)u_{t,\bar AI}=L_tA(q)L_t(r_I)u_{t,\bar AI}=L_tA(q)d_I^{-1}.$$

source.place: Coefficient comparisons preserve units and counits; agent-written unary component calculation from the specified naturality and triangle identities (Stacks 0037, definition-adjoint; 0GLL, lemma-unit-counit-relations). Calculation 3.

proof.text:
Naturality of $d$ at $b:I\to L_sM$ is
$$d_{L_sM}L_tAR_s(b)=\bar A(b)d_I.$$
Multiply on the left by $d_{L_sM}^{-1}$ and on the right by $d_I^{-1}$. Substitute $q=e_{s,M}R_s(b)$ from step 1 into step 3 to obtain
$$b_A=L_tA(e_{s,M})L_tAR_s(b)d_I^{-1}=L_tA(e_{s,M})d_{L_sM}^{-1}\bar A(b).$$

source.place: Coefficient comparisons preserve units and counits; agent-written unary component calculation from the specified naturality and triangle identities (Stacks 0037, definition-adjoint; 0GLL, lemma-unit-counit-relations). Calculation 4.

proof.text:
Suppose $b$ and $e_{s,M}$ are invertible. Functors send an inverse to an inverse: applying the functor to each of $xx^{-1}=1$ and $x^{-1}x=1$ verifies both inverse equations. Thus all three factors in step 4 are invertible. Multiplying that product on either side by
$$\bar A(b^{-1})d_{L_sM}(L_tA(e_{s,M}))^{-1}$$
cancels adjacent inverse factors and gives the identity. This proves both invertibility of $b_A$ and $b_A^{-1}=\bar A(b^{-1})a_A(M)$.

source.place: Coefficient comparisons preserve units and counits; agent-written unary component calculation from the specified naturality and triangle identities (Stacks 0037, definition-adjoint; 0GLL, lemma-unit-counit-relations). Calculation 5.

proof.text:
Let $F=L_tA$, $E_M=F(e_{s,M})$, $E_{M'}=F(e_{s,M'})$ and $H=FR_sL_s(f)$. Counit naturality gives $f e_{s,M}=e_{s,M'}R_sL_s(f)$, hence $F(f)E_M=E_{M'}H$. Both $E$ factors have inverses by the preceding functor calculation, so multiplication on the left by $E_{M'}^{-1}$ and on the right by $E_M^{-1}$ gives
$$E_{M'}^{-1}F(f)=HE_M^{-1},$$
the asserted inverse-factor identity. The morphism $f$ need not be invertible.

source.place: Coefficient comparisons preserve units and counits; agent-written unary component calculation from the specified naturality and triangle identities (Stacks 0037, definition-adjoint; 0GLL, lemma-unit-counit-relations). Calculation 6.

proof.text:
Naturality of $d$ at $L_s(f):L_sM\to L_sM'$ reads
$$d_{L_sM'}L_tAR_sL_s(f)=\bar A(L_s(f))d_{L_sM}.$$
Using step 6 and the definition of $a_A$, compute
$$a_A(M')L_tA(f)=d_{L_sM'}E_{M'}^{-1}L_tA(f)=d_{L_sM'}L_tAR_sL_s(f)E_M^{-1}=\bar A(L_s(f))a_A(M).$$

source.place: Coefficient comparisons preserve units and counits; agent-written unary component calculation from the specified naturality and triangle identities (Stacks 0037, definition-adjoint; 0GLL, lemma-unit-counit-relations). Calculation 7.

proof.text: For $q=1_{R_sI}$, the defining formula is $b=L_s(1_{R_sI})u_{s,I}=u_{s,I}$. If $e_{s,M}$ is invertible, the given triangle equation $L_s(e_{s,M})u_{s,L_sM}=1$, multiplied on the left by $L_s(e_{s,M})^{-1}$, gives $u_{s,L_sM}=L_s(e_{s,M})^{-1}$. This uses the actual specified unit.

source.place: Coefficient comparisons preserve units and counits; agent-written unary component calculation from the specified naturality and triangle identities (Stacks 0037, definition-adjoint; 0GLL, lemma-unit-counit-relations). Calculation 8.

proof.text:
Apply step 8 at $M=R_sK$ to see that $v:=u_{s,L_sR_sK}$ is invertible when $e_{s,R_sK}$ is. Unit naturality at the given isomorphism $h:L_sR_sK\to K$ is exactly
$$u_{s,K}h=L_sR_s(h)v.$$
Consequently $u_{s,K}=L_sR_s(h)v h^{-1}$, a product of isomorphisms; its inverse is $h v^{-1}L_sR_s(h^{-1})$, as verified by cancelling adjacent factors. All equations were proved inside the given categories, so no auxiliary evaluation or faithfulness assumption is needed.
